title: Paridyum region registry
description: Proposed under RFC-0014. TWO BLOCKS, deliberately separate. `jurisdictions` is the namespace — legal boundaries we intend to serve, from which nothing infrastructural is generated. `regions` is what exists; every region code must name a declared jurisdiction. A jurisdiction with no region is the normal case. The archive declared eight regions and deployed one, all eight seeded pointing at the same endpoint; that is the failure this separation prevents.

jurisdictions.description: The namespace. Adding an entry costs nothing and builds nothing.

code.description: The key, and the only identifier anything else may reference. MUST name a jurisdiction declared in `jurisdictions` — a region is a jurisdiction that has been built. Never carries a number: two locations in one jurisdiction are two datacentres by this model's own definition, so a number could only ever distinguish buildings. The archive's AWS-shaped codes are the counter-example — `ap-south-1` and `ap-south-2` are Mumbai and Hyderabad, both India, and AWS calls them two REGIONS. Immutable: tenant.region references it and ADR-0041 makes that contractual.

name.description: Human-readable, for the region picker an operator chooses from. Never parsed.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the legal jurisdiction whose law governs data held here, or EU where a supranational regime does. This is the field that makes a region a residency boundary rather than a location. EU is the case that proves the region code cannot simply be a country code: GDPR Art. 1(3) forbids restricting the free movement of personal data within the Union, so Finland, Sweden, Poland and Spain are ONE residency jurisdiction and one region. Two regions in one jurisdiction are two failure domains and should be datacentres.

continent.description: Grouping for display only. Carries no routing or legal meaning.

status.description: The ONE status authority (RFC-0014 decision 1). The archive carried this alongside a health_score column and a separate DISABLE_REGION environment CSV with nothing reconciling them, so a region could be active in the database and disabled in configuration simultaneously. There is no second switch. `degraded` and `disabled` are declared operational intent, not measured health.

control.description: Exactly one region is the control region and holds the control plane (ADR-0047 decision 1). Being the control region is not a tier and is never sold.

satisfies.description: Which territorial regime this placement addresses. ADR-0041 decision 4 forbids claiming a framework as satisfied before an audit says so, so this records what the placement is FOR, never a certification held.

datacentres.description: Failure domains inside the residency boundary. AT LEAST ONE MUST BE `live`: a region whose datacentres are all planned is a region that does not exist, and belongs in `jurisdictions` until one of them does. That is the archive's defect stated as a constraint — it declared eight regions, deployed one, and seeded all eight pointing at the same cluster-local endpoint. A count of one live datacentre also means RFC-0015 decision 3 gives this region restore-from-backup rather than fast recovery, which is why the count is per-region data rather than a platform-wide assumption.

suggest_for.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries for which this region is shown first in the picker. ORDERING ONLY. Under RFC-0015 decision 5 the operator chooses explicitly, so this may never place a tenant, and an unmapped country is not a gap. The archive mapped twenty countries of roughly two hundred and let the remainder fall to a silent default; that default is the defect this field is forbidden from reintroducing.

id.description: `<region code>-<IATA city code>-<ordinal>`, e.g. `in-mum-1`. The ordinal distinguishes buildings and nothing else. Never appears in a tenant-facing surface, a contract, or an API response — naming one there would make an operational fact contractual by accident.

status.description: Declared intent. A datacentre may be added, drained or retired without telling anyone, because it is not a term of any contract.

code.description: The code a region takes when this jurisdiction is built. Lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or a supranational code where one governs (`eu`). Never carries a number.

continent.description: Grouping for display only. Carries no legal meaning — `eu` spans a continent's subset, not the continent.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries this boundary covers. Plural because a jurisdiction may be supranational: the EEA is one boundary over many countries, which is why a region code cannot simply be a country code.

regime.description: The governing law, named. Records what the boundary IS, never that we satisfy it — ADR-0041 decision 4 forbids claiming a framework before an audit says so.

localization.description: Whether the regime forces data to stay in-country. `none` for most — transfer is permitted with safeguards. `sectoral` is the field that matters: Indonesian banking and healthcare, Indian payment data. A sectoral mandate fires on the first customer in that SECTOR, not that country, which a country-driven region plan would miss entirely.

availability.description: What a tenant-facing surface says about a jurisdiction that has NO live region (RFC-0051 §A2). Absent is the normal case and means the jurisdiction's availability is read from the regions list rather than claimed here — if a live region exists the jurisdiction is operational, and this field is meaningless. It exists because 'coming soon' is a CLAIM about intent, and STD-0021 forbids a surface manufacturing credibility it has not earned: a screen implying thirteen jurisdictions are queued, when nothing in the estate says they are, is that failure arriving through a form control. Putting the claim here makes it wrong in an artifact rather than only in a UI. `coming_soon` asserts a build is intended. `on_request` asserts none is planned and a contract could start one, and is the honest default for a jurisdiction nobody has committed to. This does NOT add a second status authority (RFC-0014 decision 1): a region's status remains the one switch, and this is a property of a jurisdiction, which has no status.
